newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Ifo west German business index up in May.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Ifo west German business index up in May.

text.p: The Ifo economic institute reported on Thursday an improvement in German business sentiment in May, providing further evidence that Europe's largest economy is on track for solid, if unspectacular recovery.
Ifo said the business climate index derived from its monthly survey rose to 95.3 in May from 94.7 in April. The modest increase was at the upper end of economists' forecasts.
"It's a good number. We are seeing an export-led recovery gaining strength," said Hans-Guenther Redeker, an economist at Chase Investment Bank in London.
Analysts also said there were signs of a gradual pickup in demand for plant and machinery which was a ray of hope for a revival in domestic demand.
The May rise marked a slowdown from April when the business climate index rose to 94.7 from 92.6. Economists attributed the slowdown to the large number of public holidays during May.

Sentiment may also have been dampened by uncertainty over European monetary union caused by the German government's controversial and unsuccessful attempt to seek a payout in 1997 from a revaluation of reserves held at the Bundesbank, economists said.
The east German business climate index fell slightly, to 103.5 from 103.6 in April.

The Ifo data had little impact on the German bond market which had already priced in a modest rise. The benchmark, 6.0 percent 10-year July 2007 bond was bid at 102.11 at 1020 GMT for a yield of 5.71 percent, little changed from Wednesday's close.
